title: Why cooking gas has become so expensive
lines: Cooking gas has become a luxury in parts of Pakistan, just as winter arrives.
The official price of LPG is two hundred and eighty rupees a kilo.
But in remote northern areas, it is reportedly selling for seven hundred to eight hundred rupees a kilo, according to Dawn.
Traders told Profit that a twelve-kilo cylinder jumped from about four thousand five hundred to seven thousand rupees within days.
Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik told the National Assembly that the closure of the Pakistan-Iran border is a major reason.
He said fifty to sixty percent of Pakistan's LPG came from Iran, and the rest from Qatar, whose supply is suspended because of the war.
The Gabd-Rimdan and Taftan crossings were closed on the seventeenth of October, citing security and anti-smuggling concerns.
Hundreds of trucks, including LPG tankers, have been stranded on both sides.
LPG matters most in areas without piped gas, where families use it to cook and keep warm.
The minister says the government is reviewing the system, and looking to bring gas in by sea from other countries.
Until then, many households face a cold and costly winter.
